1: The way out, into Warrior City.
3: A ladder down through a trapdoor. The guards call it 'the quick way to the cells.'
r: A rack of clubs. Each one has a name burned into the handle. One just says 'CLUB'.
T: The stands, packed to the top tier. Somebody's selling roast nuts. Somebody's always selling roast nuts.
+: Barnaby's desk: a speaking trumpet, a bell, and a list of names, most of them crossed out.
$: The commentator's box. Velvet, varnish, and a cushion that says LOUD.

objects.name: Barnaby Loudmouth
lines: CHEERING IS COMPULSORY!
...You too. Especially you.

objects.name: Sergeant Maelis
lines: Broken Guard. We rake the sand, we carry the fallen out, we mind the drains.
Our families have guarded a prince for five hundred years. We guard a sandbox with seats. Family tradition, of a sort.

answer: Five hundred years of names. We cross them out when they fall. It's the only writing we're allowed.
The newest line's blank. Try not to make me cross you out. I've a steady hand, but I'd rather not.
His captain wrote him down as lost in action. Not deserter. Lost.
My family's kept that word for five hundred years. Lost things can be found.
Oh, now you've done it.
The north drain runs under the wall toward the maze. Hugo found something in it once. He won't say what. Gardeners.

questions.ask: Some guard. You rake sand for a living.
answer: I do. In very straight lines. Nobody ever notices the lines.
I'll notice you, though. Long memory. Short rake.

lines: The fight card, chalked fresh every day: BRING A FIGHTER OR BRING IRON.
A smaller line at the bottom: CHEERING IS COMPULSORY.
Under that, in pencil: "whoo."

objects.name: Guard
lines: Go on. Hit him. Not me. Him.
Hey. We're not gonna mess with you.
Your friend's back down in the cells. Holding his corner, he says.

answer: Whoever's winning. I'm a guard, not a fool.
Barnaby says loyalty's for dogs and ticket holders. I've no ticket.

questions.ask: Brave words from the back row.
answer: The back row's where the brave ones sit. The front row gets sand in its teeth.
Go on, then. You hit him.

objects.name: Guard
lines: I've got two coppers on the big one. No offence.

answer: The Warden. Takes thirty strikes before he so much as blinks.
Gary from the cells says he blinked once. Nobody believes Gary. Gary doesn't care.
It's all I've got. We don't get paid. I bet the same two coppers every week.
Lost them every week, too. Still mine, in spirit.

objects.name: Guard
lines: We don't get paid enough for this.

questions.ask: How much do you get paid?
answer: Nothing. We get a seat, a spear and the smell.
Sergeant Maelis says the honour's the pay. Maelis also rakes sand in straight lines for fun.
That's the trouble. I tried quitting last spring.
Nobody noticed. So I came back. Nobody noticed that either.

objects.name: Guard
lines: Strength is valued more than anything here. Also snacks.

answer: Roast nuts from the cart by Kaldor's statue. The one that looks like a potato.
The statue, not the cart. Though the cart's not much better.

questions.ask: You look like you've had enough snacks.
answer: Strength is valued here. I am storing strength. In my middle.
You'll thank me in a famine.

objects.name: Guard
lines: Is it starting? It's starting.

answer: The fight! Barnaby's about to do his voice. The big voice.
He practises it in the tavern. Barkeep Rolla's banned him twice. He does it quieter now. Not much.
It's always about to start. That's the best bit.
...You've ruined it. It's not starting any more. Thanks.

objects.name: Guard
lines: Shh. Shh. It's starting.

answer: Him. Me. Everyone. Barnaby's about to start, and when Barnaby starts, you can hear him in the next kingdom.
If you miss the first line you miss the joke. There's always a joke. It's always about Kaldor's chin.
Shh.
...A kettle? A kettle! Shh.

objects.name: Guard
lines: I came for the warden. Everyone comes for the warden.

questions.ask: What's so great about the Warden?
answer: Thirty strikes and he doesn't move. Not a step. Not a sigh.
My wife says I should be more like him. I think she meant the not-sighing.

questions.ask: Everyone comes for the Warden. Not you.
answer: Harsh. True, but harsh.
I come for the Warden. People come for him. I come with them. That's friendship.

objects.name: Guard
lines: Mind the sand. It gets everywhere. Everywhere.

answer: Boots. Hair. Teeth. Last week I found some in a letter I hadn't opened yet.
Somewhere, someone's reading this and checking their pockets. Go on. Check.

questions.ask: You're mostly sand by now, aren't you?
answer: Forty per cent, the healer reckons. Healer Maud says it's the most interesting thing about me.
She's not wrong. That's the worst part.

objects.name: Old Mott
lines: You wouldn't want an old man fighting. I'll let you have at it!

objects.name: Nails
lines: My ice cubes melted.

objects.name: Silas Seen
lines: You're the strong silent type. You got this.

objects.name: Brannoc
lines: Zzz...
(He's out cold. A snot bubble swells and shrinks.)

objects.name: Brannoc
lines: Whoa. Did you do that?

intro.speaker: Barnaby Loudmouth
lines: HEAR YE! In this corner: a stranger! In the other corner: FIVE OF THE KING'S OWN!
Nobody here is paid. Everybody here is angry about it. FIGHT!

intro.speaker: Barnaby Loudmouth
lines: Oh, you've done it now. You've woken up THE WARDEN!
Thirty strikes, they say. Nobody's ever counted past twelve. FIGHT!
